newsitem.title: USA: Study backs single shot for ear infections.
newsitem.headline: Study backs single shot for ear infections.

text.p: A single shot of an antibiotic for children with ear infections works as well as 10 days of swallowing medicine, according to a study published on Monday.
The report was based on a 484 children ages three months to three years who suffered from acute ear infections, the most common health problem among young children.
In the United States such infections have been traditionally treated with an oral antimicrobial agent taken for 10 days.

The study, published in "Pediatrics," the monthly journal of the American Academy of Pediatrics, found that a single injection of ceftriaxone worked as well as 10 days of oral treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

The report, from Boston City Hospital and Boston University, said the single dose approach might address problems of incomplete therapy with oral treatment that often comes from children who won't take the medicine or can't keep it down, and parents who forget to give it to them.
